items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: See you in a hundred years.
That familiar voice from a hundred years ago fades in the wind. Before the Mei tree, a figure materializes.
The image grows more solid and vivid, exactly as Reed saw in the memories.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Heron!
As her form solidifies, Reed can't suppress a gasp.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I-I get it now. Those Wind Knots were frozen by the power of the Longevity Sword, that's why the Windweave's been experiencing so much interference.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: And Heron, she's been trapped here for all these years?

items.speaker: Mule
items.text: Bray!
The mule trots out happily, eager to bring its friends, old and new, together at last.
Seeing Reed frozen in place, it gently tugs at her, taking a blade of grass on her head into its mouth.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Stop that. She's not a snack.
She laughs. The old mule reluctantly trots aside and lingers behind the Mei tree.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: It is good to finally see you in person, Reedit.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I sincerely apologize for the trouble. There was little I could do from within the seal. You look well, though. I'm glad.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: When you said you'd find me, I didn't think you meant like this.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: It was you, wasn't it? The wind, the paper notes, you used them to guide me here, didn't you?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I did. I believe you've seen this little Qi trick a few times by now.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Within the seal, I was unable to communicate with the outside world, until those curious strings were put up.
She raises her finger and points first at the old Mei tree and then at the telephone pole standing next to its canopy.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: An odd Qi runs through them, one I found I could control. That's how I got on the forum.
Reed listens, making mental notes of her questions, until she arrives at a realization.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Strings? You mean the cables? You're telling me you can connect to the Internet through Qi?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: It is a remarkable technology. Though at times, the Qi would disappear.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: When that happened, I could no longer reach you.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Well, as much as I'd like to dive into it—I really, really would—let's save it for another time, kinda on a deadline here.
She stops and stares at Paper Heron.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I did what you asked, Heron. I untied all the knots.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Now it's time for you to hold up your end of the deal.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Only, you said that the Method would die along with the sword. So, you never really planned on passing it on to me, huh?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Or by "teach me," did you mean showing me your story in the Wind Knots?
She studies Reed. Her smile and tone are just as Reed remembers—light and warm.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You are so very much like her.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Her?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Mayfly. She too was a reed, sprouting in spring, withering by winter.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: And just like her, you move with haste in every single moment.
A name that they both know lingers in the air, stirring up memories and melancholy.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Mayfly ...

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: That's why I reached out when I saw your post. Fate really seems determined to bring your kind to me.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: There's one last knot. I want you to be the one to undo it.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Another one? But didn't I already ...

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: The story has yet to come to an end. The Method of Longevity didn't truly die with the sword.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: When I shattered it, I truly didn't expect I'd ever wake again. I thought the Method of Longevity would die with me.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: And even less that I'd be awakened by this new Qi.
With a sigh, she brushes the old Mei tree as if closing a door behind her.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: The sword may be gone, but it was nothing more than a vessel. Now that I've returned, the Method of Longevity lives on.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: And I shall pass it on to you, as thanks for your help.
Her heartbeat quickens in her chest.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Don't be afraid. It sounds complicated, but it only takes a moment to grasp.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You've returned me to life. Please, allow me to extend yours.
She smiles and extends her hand, then nods to Reed.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Now, give me your hand.
The answer she has pursued across lifetimes finally within reach.
Yet now that it's here, Reed feels an inexplicable panic.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Are you ... Are you for real, like, really real?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Having second thoughts?
Reed touches her own hair with anxiety. More blades of grass, each one growing yellower with each passing day, fall to the ground.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I would never wish to pressure you. An offer like this could take time to process.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Perhaps you feel differently about longevity now, after seeing what happened to Mayfly.
Paper Heron withdraws her hand and waits for Reed's answer.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Do you still wish for more time in this world, little reed?
She reflects on the question for a long while. A moment later, she raises her head slowly and firmly.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I do.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I know my time's short, but I still have a life to live, just like anyone else, and I have the right to live as long as I can.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Even if it's hard, even if it's impossible, I can't stop just because I'm scared.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I want to live, to see more, write more, experience more.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I'll do anything to have one more day, one more hour, even one more minute to live.
She steps forward with growing certainty.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I know that the "me" who sprouts next spring will be "me" in some way, but she'll never be "me." My goals, my experiences, my thoughts, my work ... They'll be lost forever.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: And even if that Reed continues to sprout across a thousand lives, it will never be me again.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: So I'll keep looking, till my last leaves have withered away.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: At least then, I can go without any regrets.
Paper Heron's response begins with surprise, but soon, her face adopts that familiar smile, serene and wistful.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Well said!

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Many have held back for fear of the risks. It's rare to see someone with such remarkable courage.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I am glad to have at last found the right person.
She extends her hand a second time, offering Reed a sincere invitation.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Then repeat after me: In the vastness between heaven and earth, all things will bow to my measure.
Reed reaches for the ending and answer she has yearned for. Her fingers meet the rough bark.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: In   the   vastness   between   heaven   and   earth,   all   things   will   bow   to   my   measure.
Frozen wind cascades from her fingertips, then begins to flow.
Suddenly, the illusion before her eyes shatters. Another unexpected figure emerges from within, laughing.
Ahahaha ... Finally, after all this time!
The figure beneath the Mei tree brushes away the ash from her shoulder.
Reed steps back in shock. The name falters on her tongue, as if she's unable to believe it herself.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: You-You're Rén!

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Indeed. Now, come and pay respect to your master.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: So it was you who sent those messages on the forum, not Heron?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: And I've, I've just ...
Reed staggers, the depth of her mistake striking her with the force of a heavy blow.
Master Rén's smile grows mad and overwide, unconcerned by her fear.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: There's no need to be afraid. I may have used Paper Heron's name to bring you here, but I did not lie about the Method of Longevity. I will guide you to it, if you wish.
She reaches for Reed's forehead.
But her hand meets nothing but air.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: You-You did all this to bring me here, just to make me your student? Why?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: What're you trying to do?
Her question is met with a mocking laugh.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Hmph. I had hoped you were wise enough to not mistake my kindness for malice.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: All this fuss over a borrowed name, and yet you overlook the truth. I am your only hope to attain longevity.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Everything has a price. If longevity is what you desire, you must take the risk and pay it.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: I came so close back then. Lǎnzhū would have been long dead if Heron hadn't stood in my way.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: I never thought she would be mad enough to shatter her school's legacy just to seal me away.
The rising wind nearly swallows up her words.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: So much time has passed. None who remember those days now live. Only you and I.
But now even the howl of the wind is lost beneath the roar of cracking earth.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: All those lives wasted because of her!

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: You're not gonna ...
Ignoring Reed's shock, Master Rén flicks her sleeve sharply, and a patch of ground near the Mei tree's roots sinks.
Water surges from the cracks between rock and soil, carrying panicked fish along with it.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: If those "cables" hadn't been built, I wouldn't have awoken so soon. For that, I am grateful.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Ahahaha ... I should thank you, too, for untying those knots and freeing me from the seal.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: You see, unlike Master Heron, I ensure those who aid me are properly repaid.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Come here.
She yanks Reed close. Qi gathers in her right hand as she aims at the newly formed lake.
Leaves fall like rain from the tree as the earth buckles. Ripples bounce across the water.
And the water continues to rise.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Today the beast will fall, and I will ascend triumphant.
The lake overflows, soaking the parched yellow grass around it. The chaos of the scene matches the mounting panic surging through Reed's body.
Forgetting everything else, she grabs at Master Rén's arm.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Stop! You can't do this!

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Rén!
She stumbles, almost falling into the lake.
Just as the visions showed, Lǎnzhū's eyes were once a lake at this very spot.
Now after centuries of slumber, it awakens.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I can't let her ...
The wind cries.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: ... destroy the city.
A gale rushes toward the center of the lake.
Signs and awnings, bikes and roof shingles, everything the wind touches is pulled up in the rush.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I have to do something.
But she can't reach her.
It's too late now.
No need to worry.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Huh?
Somewhere in the groaning of the wind, she catches a faint, familiar voice.
Every creature, whether beast or man, wishes for more time in this world.

But know this: Those at their peak will decline, and those that have fallen will rise, for it is the Way to take from those in excess and give to those who lack. When Lǎnzhū sleeps, the world around it thrives; when it awakens, the world falls into ruin. All is in balance.
The workings of Heaven remain constant. There is no need to stop her.
Reed doesn't answer. She forces herself forward, the grass blades on her head bending flat against the fierce wind.
She strains with all her might, but Master Rén has already raised her hand, ready to strike.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: It's too late. The beast ends today, and your mission with it.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Haaah!

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Lǎnzhū has awakened.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: The beast is weak. But my Qi, it flows out from me.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: What have you done, Heron?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: I will never ...

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Eight   views   merge,   the   mystery   of   Qi.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Three   lights   darken,   and   all   lose   their   way.
